name: Wayfair Inc.
moat_justification: Largest pure-play online home-goods retailer with real scale assets — CastleGate bulky-parcel logistics, a deep third-party supplier/selection network, 21.7M active customers with 80.2% of Q2 2026 orders from repeat customers, and specialty/luxury brands (Perigold +35% in Q2 2026) — but no demonstrated return on capital and no pricing power in the numbers: gross margin has been flat at ~30% for four years (28.0% FY2022, 30.6% FY2023, 30.2% FY2024, 30.2% FY2025, 30.1% TTM in fundamentals.json), book equity is negative (-$2,782M at FY2025) so the roic_proxy series is denominator noise (-49.0% FY2020, +236.1% FY2022, -1.4% FY2025), and conservative owner's earnings were positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years. Consumers face near-zero switching costs against Amazon, Walmart, IKEA and the big-box chains. A 4 gives CAP 7.2 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 6.5%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.8% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.6x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 7.2x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Turnaround online home-goods leader, moat 4/10 — TTM owner's earnings just turned positive ($1.95/share, 1.8% yield) but at $107.28 the weighted IRR is only 5.0% (weighted IV@15% $20.34, even super-bull 7.7%); it clears 15% only below ~$20 — Tier D.
moat_for: Scale pure-play in online home goods: $12,457M FY2025 revenue, 21.7M active customers, repeat customers placed 80.2% of Q2 2026 orders
CastleGate specialized logistics for bulky / large-parcel delivery — the category generalists handle worst
Supplier and selection network plus house / specialty brands (Perigold grew >35% in Q2 2026, specialty brands ~20%) with higher-margin mix
Share capture in a fragmented market: Q2 2026 revenue +7.5% YoY (U.S. +8.7%) while the home category was roughly flat-to-down
moat_against: No pricing power in the filed numbers: gross margin flat at ~30% FY2023-2025 (30.6% / 30.2% / 30.2%) despite scale gains; promotion- and paid-search-driven demand
No demonstrated returns on capital: book equity negative (-$2,782M FY2025), roic_proxy is denominator noise, owner's earnings positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years
Near-zero consumer switching costs; Amazon, Walmart, IKEA, Home Depot / Lowe's all attack the same basket with larger logistics and balance sheets
SBC-driven dilution: diluted share count 106M (FY2022) → 128M (FY2025) → 131M (current YTD), +6.5%/yr CAGR; SBC was $605M in FY2023 and still $307M TTM
Levered, cyclical: net debt $1,796M plus $1,025M lease liabilities against a just-positive OE base; demand tracks housing turnover and discretionary spend, and imports carry tariff exposure
